Snapshot: Willowmere builds a ticket-deflection layer used by mid-market help desks (SaaS). Primary objective: push >40% of incoming tickets to self-serve via RAG-powered support agent and deflection widgets.

Scale/requirements (customer-provided):
- Document base: ~18M historical tickets + KB + product docs (~250GB compressed text). Expect ~20M vectors after chunking.
- Target query latency: P95 end-to-end <= 150ms for vector retrieval + rerank top-5; absolute P99 budget 350ms (hard).
- Throughput: average 200 qps peak bursts to 800 qps during incident windows.
- Cost target: goal <= $0.05 / query (including embedding lookup + reranker). High sensitivity.
- Quality: top-5 reranked results must have >95% helpful rate on internal evals (human evals on 2k prompts).

Architecture preferences / constraints:
- Prefer dedicated instances (VPC) due to customer data mix and SSO/SAML integration; data residency US-only.
- Candidate retrieval: approximate nearest neighbor (FAISS/HNSW) + hybrid BM25 fallback for noisy queries. Looking at Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching + cache TTLs.
- Embeddings: want compact 768-d embeddings, willing to try quantized indexes (8-bit) for cost. Ask for recommended embedding model from Redwood catalog and expected per-vector storage after PQ.
- Reranker: cross-encoder small model for top-5 re-ranking; conversation-level context must be included (3 previous turns). Need kernel selection guidance to hit latency SLOs.

Operational asks from evaluation:
- 2-week POC with a dedicated pool sized to simulate peak (2x A100 equiv), ingest ~2M sample docs (subset) and run synthetic traffic to validate P95/P99.
- Provide a per-query cost model with breakdown: embeddings, vector search, reranking, token generation.
- Show caching strategy for repeated queries (prefix & KV cache) and estimate unit economics improvements.

- SE notes: "Tight SLO + large index is the main risk; need to demo real tail latency under load."

- Deflection lift >= 30% in simulated routing tests.
- Per-query cost projection <= $0.05 at production scale (18M docs, expected 200 qps average).
